q.s: The two rows of six granaries each, along with Cemetery H, were found at which Harappan site?
q.x: Harappa (on the Ravi) has the two rows of six granaries and Cemetery H; the dockyard is at Lothal.

q.s: Which of the following finds is NOT from Harappa?
q.x: The dockyard is at Lothal; the granaries and Cemeteries H and R-37 are at Harappa.

q.s: The bronze 'Dancing Girl' of Mohenjodaro was made by the technique of:
q.x: The Dancing Girl shows that the Harappans knew lost-wax (cire perdue) casting, long before the Chola bronzes.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Harappan metal craft is correct?
o: Lost-wax casting began in India only with the Chola bronzes
The Dancing Girl shows the Harappans knew lost-wax casting
The Daimabad figures are made of iron
The Harappans did not know copper
q.x: Lost-wax casting goes back to the Harappan Dancing Girl; Harappans used copper and bronze but not iron.

q.s: The typical pottery of the Harappan Civilisation was:
o: Red ware with black painted designs
q.x: Harappan pottery was wheel-made red ware painted in black; Painted Grey Ware belongs to the Vedic age.

q.s: Which of the following has NOT been found at Mohenjodaro?
q.x: Wall paintings are not found at Mohenjodaro; the other three are its famous finds.

q.s: In the Later Vedic period, the royal officer who collected taxes such as bali and bhaga was the:
q.x: The Bhagadugha was the collector of taxes in the Later Vedic period.

q.s: In the Later Vedic period, bhaga was a compulsory share of the produce, usually amounting to:
q.x: Bhaga was the king's compulsory share, usually one-sixth of the produce, not a voluntary offering.

q.s: Which Vedic texts deal with the measurement and construction of sacrificial altars?
q.x: The Sulba Sutras (by Baudhayana, Apastamba, Katyayana) deal with altar geometry; Dharma Sutras deal with law and duty.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an author of a Sulbasutra?
q.x: Baudhayana, Apastamba and Katyayana wrote Sulbasutras; Panini was the grammarian of the Ashtadhyayi.

q.s: In a Vedic sacrifice, the Adhvaryu priest was associated with the:
q.x: The Adhvaryu performed the ritual acts using the Yajurveda; the Hotri recited the Rigveda and the Udgatri chanted the Samaveda.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Vedic priest and Veda is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Adhvaryu belonged to the Yajurveda; the Udgatri chanted the Samaveda.

q.s: Which inscription records the depositing of money with guilds at fixed interest?
q.x: The Nashik inscription records deposits with guilds invested at interest, showing that guilds acted as banks.

q.s: Which of the following statements about guilds in ancient India is correct?
o: Guilds were abolished by the Satavahanas
Guilds existed only in the Gupta period
Guilds also acted as banks, taking deposits at interest
q.x: Inscriptions such as Nashik record money deposited with guilds at interest.

q.s: The second urbanisation in the Ganga plain (6th century BCE) was made possible mainly by the use of:
q.x: Iron tools made forest clearance and surplus farming possible, leading to towns in the Ganga plain.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the second urbanisation in the Ganga plain?
q.x: The second urbanisation rested on iron, NBPW and punch-marked coins; bronze was the metal of the Harappan (first) urbanisation.

q.s: Who among the following was a major Buddhist logician?
q.x: Dignaga was the great Buddhist logician; Dharmakirti developed his tradition.

q.s: Aryadeva, a Buddhist philosopher, was a disciple of:
q.x: Aryadeva was Nagarjuna's disciple in the Madhyamika school; Yogachara is linked to Asanga and Vasubandhu.

q.s: The doctrine of Sunyata (emptiness) is associated with which Buddhist school?
q.x: Nagarjuna's Madhyamika school taught Sunyata.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a school of Buddhist philosophy?
q.x: Nyaya is an orthodox (astika) Hindu school of logic; the others are Buddhist schools.

q.s: The Charvaka school of philosophy accepted which of the following as the only valid means of knowledge?
q.x: The Charvakas accepted only perception (pratyaksha) and rejected inference.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Charvaka school is correct?
o: It accepted the authority of the Vedas
It accepted inference as a valid means of knowledge
It is known mainly through its rivals' criticism
It believed in rebirth and karma
q.x: Charvaka texts are lost; we know the school mainly from works such as Madhava's Sarvadarshanasangraha.

q.s: The Gupta era (Gupta Samvat) began in:
q.x: The Gupta era of 319-320 CE marks the accession of Chandragupta I; 78 CE is the Saka era and 57 BCE the Vikrama era.

q.s: The first Gupta ruler to take the title Maharajadhiraja was:
q.x: Chandragupta I was the first to take the title Maharajadhiraja; Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha were only Maharajas.

q.s: The Mehrauli Iron Pillar inscription refers to a king called 'Chandra', who is identified with:
q.x: The 'Chandra' of the Mehrauli pillar is identified with Chandragupta II Vikramaditya.

q.s: Which of the following names or titles is NOT associated with Chandragupta II?
q.x: Devanampiya ('beloved of the gods') was Ashoka's title; the others are linked to Chandragupta II.

q.s: In Gupta administration, the bhukti (province) was headed by the:
q.x: The bhukti was under the Uparika, the vishaya (district) under the Vishayapati and the village under the Gramika.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Gupta administration is correct?
o: Officials were paid by land grants as well as in cash
The vishaya was headed by the Gramika
Samudragupta annexed every kingdom he defeated
Officials were paid only in gold dinaras
q.x: Land grants to officials grew in the Gupta period; Samudragupta reinstated many defeated kings as feudatories.

q.s: In ancient India, the tax paid in cash (gold) instead of produce was known as:
q.x: Hiranya was the tax paid in cash; Sita was the produce of crown land.

q.s: Which of the following ancient revenue terms is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Sita was the produce of crown lands collected in kind; Hiranya was the cash tax.

q.s: Tamralipti, the chief eastern port of the Gupta period, was located in:
q.x: Tamralipti (Tamluk) was the eastern port in Bengal; Bharuch was the western port.

q.s: The ancient western port of Bhrigukachchha (Bharuch) was located at the mouth of the river:
q.x: Bharuch stood at the mouth of the Narmada.

q.s: Amarasimha, one of the Navaratnas of the court of Vikramaditya, is known for:
q.x: Amarasimha compiled the Sanskrit lexicon Amarakosha; Brihat Samhita is by Varahamihira.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the Navaratnas of the court of Vikramaditya?
q.x: The Navaratnas included Kalidasa, Amarasimha, Varahamihira, Dhanvantari and others; Aryabhata is not in the list.

q.s: In the Battle of Takkolam (949 CE), the Chola king Parantaka I was defeated by:
q.x: Takkolam was a Chola defeat: the Rashtrakuta Krishna III beat Parantaka I.

q.s: The Chola-Chalukya wars were fought largely over the control of:
q.x: Both the Cholas and the Western Chalukyas backed rival claimants to Vengi in coastal Andhra.

q.s: The Uttaramerur inscriptions describing village assemblies belong to the reign of the Chola king:
q.x: The Uttaramerur inscriptions are dated 919 and 921 CE, in the reign of Parantaka I.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Uttaramerur inscriptions is correct?
o: They made sabha members hold office for life
They lay down qualifications and disqualifications for sabha members
They belong to the reign of Rajaraja I
They describe a non-brahmadeya ur village
q.x: They set out qualifications, kudavolai election and recall; members served one-year terms.

q.s: The Vijayanagara kingdom was founded in the year:
q.x: Vijayanagara was founded in 1336; the Bahmani kingdom followed in 1347.

q.s: Who recaptured Warangal from the Tughlaqs in 1336?
q.x: Kapaya Nayaka, successor of Prolaya Nayaka, recaptured Warangal in 1336.

q.s: Rana Sanga defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the battle of:
q.x: Rana Sanga defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Khatoli; Khanua (1527) was Babur's victory over Sanga.

q.s: Ibrahim Lodi was defeated and killed by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat in:
q.x: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat on 21 April 1526.

q.s: The Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi, a department of agriculture, was set up by:
q.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq created the Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi to extend cultivation.

q.s: Which of the following departments was NOT created by Firoz Tughlaq?
q.x: Diwan-i-Mustakhraj (arrears of revenue) was Alauddin Khalji's; the other three were Firoz Tughlaq's.

q.s: The Khalji revolution of 1290 is significant in the history of the Delhi Sultanate because it:
o: Opened high office to non-Turks and Indian Muslims
Ended the rule of the Sultanate
q.x: The Khalji revolution broke the Turkish monopoly of high office.

q.s: Under the Lodis, the Sultan's position in relation to the Afghan nobles was that of:
q.x: The Lodi Sultan was only 'first among equals' among the Afghan nobles.

q.s: The Diwan-i-Bandagan, a separate department of slaves, was created by:
q.x: Firoz Tughlaq, who had about 1,80,000 slaves, created the Diwan-i-Bandagan.

q.s: Which of the following statements about slavery in medieval India is correct?
o: Slavery was unknown in the Vijayanagara empire
Alauddin Khalji's third market dealt in horses, slaves and cattle
q.x: The 1,80,000 slaves belonged to Firoz Tughlaq; Vijayanagara slavery was called Benabaga.

q.s: Babur took the title 'Ghazi' after his victory in the battle of:
q.x: Babur took the title Ghazi after defeating Rana Sanga at Khanwa (1527).

q.s: Which of the following battles was NOT fought by Babur?
q.x: Babur fought Panipat (1526), Khanwa (1527), Chanderi (1528) and Ghaghra (1529); Talikota (1565) was fought by the Deccan Sultanates against Vijayanagara.

q.s: Rana Amar Singh of Mewar accepted Mughal suzerainty by a treaty in 1615 during the reign of:
q.x: Mewar never submitted to Akbar; Amar Singh made peace with Jahangir in 1615.

q.s: The Battle of Haldighati (1576) was fought between the Mughal army of Akbar and:
q.x: At Haldighati (1576) Man Singh led Akbar's army against Rana Pratap.

q.s: The Red Fort of Delhi was built as the core of Shah Jahan's new city of:
q.x: The Red Fort was the citadel of Shahjahanabad; Din Panah was Humayun's and Siri Alauddin's.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT built by Shah Jahan?
q.x: Agra Fort was begun by Akbar in 1565, with Kasim Khan as architect.

q.s: The Alvars of Tamil Nadu were devotees of:
q.x: The twelve Alvars were Vaishnavas; the sixty-three Nayanars were Shaivas.

q.s: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham, the hymns of the Alvars, was compiled by:
q.x: Nathamuni compiled the Divya Prabandham; Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the Shaiva Tirumurai.

q.s: Bammera Potana is famous for writing in Telugu the:
q.x: Potana wrote the Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu (8 of its 12 skandhas); the Mahabharata was by the Kavitrayam.

q.s: The Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu was first printed in 1840 by:
q.x: C.P. Brown printed Potana's Bhagavatamu in 1840.

q.s: Which of the following European powers was the first to come to India and the last to leave?
q.x: The Portuguese came first (1498) and left last (Goa, Daman and Diu freed in 1961).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Dutch East India Company (VOC) is correct?
o: It is widely called the first joint-stock company to sell shares to the public
It was the first European company to reach India
It was the last European power to leave India
q.x: The VOC (1602) sold shares to the public; the Portuguese came first and left last.

q.s: Under Dutch rule, Pulicat on the Coromandel coast became a centre of the slave trade to:
q.x: The Dutch shipped slaves from Pulicat to Batavia (Jakarta).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Dutch in Andhra is NOT correct?
o: They were the first Europeans in Andhra to mint coins
Pulicat was a hub of their slave trade to Batavia
Koringa was their chief jute centre
Saltpetre for their trade came mainly from Bihar
q.x: Koringa was known for shipbuilding; Chittavalasa was the jute centre.

q.s: Andhra weavers preferred to sell to the Dutch, Portuguese and French rather than the English mainly because the English:
o: Paid less and demanded high quality
q.x: The English used dadni advances through dubashes, paid less and demanded high quality.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the English trade with Andhra weavers is correct?
o: The English made dadni advances through dubashes
The English paid the weavers more than the Dutch
The English bought no cloth in Andhra
The weavers preferred to sell to the English
q.x: The English paid less and demanded high quality, so weavers preferred the other companies.

q.s: The Revolt of 1857 broke out at Meerut on:
q.x: The sepoys rose at Meerut on 10 May and reached Delhi on 11 May; Kanpur rose on 5 June.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of 1857 centre and the date the rising began is NOT correct?
q.x: Kanpur rose on 5 June 1857; 11 May is when the rebels reached Delhi.

q.s: The decisive battle of the Third Carnatic War, in which Eyre Coote defeated the French, was fought at:
q.x: Eyre Coote defeated Lally at Wandiwash in 1760.

q.s: A basic weakness of the French East India Company during the Carnatic Wars was that it:
o: Was a state concern dependent on the king
q.x: The French Company was state-controlled, the king holding over 60% of the shares, so it lacked initiative and funds.

q.s: During the Second Anglo-Mysore War, the British bought off the Nizam from Haidar Ali's alliance by giving him:
q.x: The British won over the Nizam with Guntur and made the Treaty of Salbai (1782) with the Marathas.

q.s: The Second Anglo-Mysore War was ended by the Treaty of:
q.x: The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) ended the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

q.s: The Dual Government in Bengal was introduced by:
q.x: Clive introduced the Dual Government (1765), which Warren Hastings ended in 1772.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Dual Government in Bengal is correct?
o: It was introduced by Warren Hastings
Under it the Nawab held the Diwani
It was abolished by Lord Cornwallis
q.x: Clive introduced it in 1765 and Warren Hastings ended it in 1772.

q.s: The first state to accept Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance (1798) was:
q.x: Hyderabad signed in 1798; Tanjore (1799), Awadh (1801) and the Peshwa (1802) followed.

q.s: Which of the following did NOT accept Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance?
q.x: Ranjit Singh never accepted it; Hyderabad, Tanjore, Awadh and the Peshwa did.

q.s: The first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833 was:
q.x: The 1833 Act made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India; Bentinck was the first.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Charter Act of 1833?
o: The Governor-General of Bengal became Governor-General of India
Laws were to continue to be called Regulations
The Company's tea and China trade monopoly ended
No Indian was to be barred from office by religion or birth
q.x: From 1833 the laws were called Acts, not Regulations.

q.s: Under the 'Tinkathiya' system in Champaran, peasants were forced to grow indigo on:
q.x: Tinkathiya meant growing indigo on 3 kathas of every 20, i.e. 3/20 of the holding.

q.s: Which of the following commercial crops is NOT correctly matched with its feature?
q.x: Tea was grown mainly in Assam; cotton in the Deccan, Gujarat and Berar.

q.s: The last famine commission of the colonial period was the:
q.x: The Woodhead Commission (1944) enquired into the Bengal famine of 1943.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a famine commission of colonial India?
q.x: The Hunter Commission dealt with education (1882) and the Punjab disturbances (1919); the others were famine commissions.

q.s: India's first telegraph line, opened in 1851 under W.B. O'Shaughnessy, ran between:
q.x: The first experimental telegraph line (1851) linked Calcutta and Diamond Harbour.

q.s: The Post Office Act of 1854 is important because it introduced:
q.x: The 1854 Act brought uniform postage rates regardless of distance, and postage stamps.

q.s: The first Municipal Corporation in India was set up in 1688 at:
q.x: Madras got the first municipal corporation in 1688; Bombay and Calcutta followed in 1726.

q.s: The Lottery Committee (1817) of the British Rule was related to:
q.x: The Lottery Committee used lottery funds for town planning in Calcutta.

q.s: The first Indian to qualify for the Indian Civil Service was:
q.x: Satyendranath Tagore qualified in 1863 and served in the Bombay Presidency.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Indian Civil Service is correct?
o: Satyendranath Tagore served in the Bengal Presidency
Lord Lytton raised the maximum age to 23
Surendranath Banerjea, selected in 1869, was later dismissed from service
R.C. Dutt was the first Indian to join the ICS
q.x: Banerjea was dismissed for a minor error; Tagore served in Bombay and Lytton cut the age to 19.

q.s: Which of the following features is NOT correctly matched with the Act that introduced it?
o: Discussion of the budget - Indian Councils Act, 1892
Dyarchy in the provinces - Indian Councils Act, 1909
Bicameralism at the Centre - Government of India Act, 1919
Dyarchy at the Centre - Government of India Act, 1935
q.x: Provincial dyarchy came with the 1919 Act; the 1909 Act brought separate electorates and the elective principle.

q.s: The first Indian to be appointed to the Viceroy's Executive Council under the Indian Councils Act, 1909 was:
q.x: Satyendra Prasanna Sinha became the Law Member under the Morley-Minto reforms.

q.s: The Indian National Trade Union Congress (INTUC) was set up by the Congress in:
q.x: INTUC was founded by the Congress in May 1947; the AITUC dated from 1920.

q.s: The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) was founded in 1920 with its first president as:
q.x: Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the first AITUC session at Bombay in 1920.

q.s: The children's magazine 'Chandamama' (1947) was started by:
q.x: Chandamama was launched in July 1947 by B. Nagireddy and Chakrapani.

q.s: Which of the following publications is NOT correctly matched with its founder?
q.x: Telugu Zenana was Rayasam Venkata Sivudu's.

q.s: The split in the Arya Samaj in 1893 separated the College Party from the Gurukul Party; Lala Hansraj and Lala Lajpat Rai belonged to the:
q.x: Hansraj and Lajpat Rai led the College (DAV) Party; Munshi Ram (Swami Shraddhanand) led the Gurukul Party.

q.s: The Gurukul at Kangri near Haridwar was set up in 1902 by:
q.x: Munshi Ram founded the Gurukul Kangri in 1902; the DAV at Lahore dates from 1886.

q.s: The Ramakrishna Mission was founded by Swami Vivekananda in the year:
q.x: The Mission was founded on 1 May 1897 at Calcutta; 1893 was the Chicago address.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Ramakrishna Mission is correct?
o: It was founded by Ramakrishna Paramahansa himself
Its motto is 'Atmano Mokshartham Jagad Hitaya Cha'
It was founded at Chicago in 1893
q.x: Vivekananda founded it in 1897; its headquarters is Belur Math.

q.s: In 1908, Bal Gangadhar Tilak was sentenced to six years' imprisonment and deported to:
q.x: Tilak served his sentence in Mandalay, where he wrote the Gita Rahasya; he was released in 1914.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Tilak's Home Rule League is correct?
o: It was founded in April 1916 with Joseph Baptista as president
It was founded in 1916 with Annie Besant as president
It was founded in 1914 at Madras
It was founded after the Lucknow Pact of 1919
q.x: Tilak's league (April 1916, Belgaum) had Joseph Baptista as president; Annie Besant led her own league from September 1916.

q.s: Which of the following revolutionary societies is NOT correctly matched with its place of origin?
q.x: The Bharat Mata Society was founded in Punjab by Ajit Singh.

q.s: Which revolutionary society was founded by V.D. Savarkar at Nasik in 1899?
q.x: Savarkar's Mitra Mela (1899) became Abhinav Bharat in 1904.

q.s: During his visit to Vijayawada on 8 April 1919, Gandhi's speech against the Rowlatt Act was translated by:
q.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao translated Gandhi's Vijayawada speech.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Rowlatt Satyagraha in Andhra is correct?
o: The hartal of 6 April 1919 was observed peacefully in Andhra towns
The Andhra Patrika supported the Rowlatt Act
Gandhi did not visit Andhra in 1919
It was led in Andhra by the Justice Party
q.x: The hartal was peaceful at Visakhapatnam, Rajahmundry, Guntur and Vijayawada; the Andhra Patrika opposed the Act.

q.s: The committee appointed to inquire into the Jallianwala Bagh massacre was headed by:
q.x: The Hunter Committee inquired into the massacre; the Rowlatt Committee led to the Rowlatt Act.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Hunter Committee is correct?
o: It sentenced General Dyer to imprisonment
Its Indian members wrote a minority report more critical of Dyer
It was appointed by the Indian National Congress
q.x: Three Indian members wrote a minority report; Dyer was only censured and relieved of command.

q.s: Gandhi began the Salt Satyagraha by breaking the salt law at Dandi on:
q.x: The march began at Sabarmati on 12 March, reached Dandi on 5 April, and Gandhi broke the law on 6 April 1930.

q.s: Dandi, where Gandhi broke the salt law, is a coastal village in which district of Gujarat?
q.x: Dandi lies in Navsari district.

q.s: The Communal Award of 1932 was announced by British Prime Minister:
q.x: Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award in August 1932.

q.s: Gandhi's fast against the Communal Award ended with the signing of the:
q.x: The Poona Pact (September 1932) replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes with reserved seats.

q.s: Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die' for the Quit India Movement at Gowalia Tank in:
q.x: The Quit India resolution was passed at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among Gandhi's Quit India instructions of August 1942?
o: Soldiers should not fire on their compatriots
Government servants should resign at once
Princes should accept the sovereignty of their people
Peasants should pay rent only to anti-government zamindars
q.x: Government servants were told not to resign but to declare their allegiance to the Congress.

q.s: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946), the Union of India was to deal with only:
q.x: The Union was to have only Defence, Foreign Affairs and Communications; residuary powers were with the provinces.

q.s: Which of the following provinces was NOT placed in Section B of the Cabinet Mission Plan?
q.x: Section B had Punjab, NWFP and Sindh; Bengal and Assam formed Section C.

q.s: The first police station attacked by Alluri Sitarama Raju during the Rampa rebellion (22 August 1922) was at:
q.x: Raju attacked Chintapalli first; he was shot at Koyyuru in 1924 and his samadhi is at Krishnadevipeta.

q.s: Which of the following places is NOT correctly matched with the Rampa rebellion of Alluri Sitarama Raju?
o: Peddagaddapalem - first defeat of Raju's forces
q.x: Krishnadevipeta is where Raju's samadhi stands; Chintapalli was the first station attacked.

q.s: Which leader resigned his professorship in 1930 and led the kisan movement in Andhra?
q.x: N.G. Ranga became the leader of the peasant movement in Andhra.

q.s: Which of the following leaders is NOT correctly matched with the region of his work?
q.x: Poet-revolutionary Kesari Singh Barahath belonged to Shahpura in Rajasthan.

q.s: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated by Nathuram Godse on:
q.x: Gandhi was shot at Birla House, Delhi, on 30 January 1948.

q.s: After independence, Gandhi wanted the Indian National Congress to be dissolved and turned into a:
q.x: In his last will Gandhi proposed turning the Congress into a Lok Sevak Sangh.

q.s: The office of Rajpramukh was abolished by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act of:
q.x: The Seventh Amendment (1956) abolished the Rajpramukh and the Part A/B/C/D classification.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT done by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956?
o: Adding the word 'Secular' to the Preamble
Replacing Part A/B/C/D States with States and Union Territories
q.x: 'Secular' was added by the 42nd Amendment (1976).

q.s: Panchayat Raj was introduced in Andhra Pradesh on:
q.x: Andhra Pradesh introduced it on 1 November 1959, second after Rajasthan (2 October 1959).

q.s: Which of the following statements about Panchayat Raj in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh was the first State to introduce it
It was introduced when Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was Chief Minister
It was introduced under Damodaram Sanjivayya
q.x: AP introduced it on 1 November 1959 under Neelam Sanjiva Reddy, after Rajasthan.

q.s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956, a statutory Regional Council for Telangana's development was to have:
q.x: The Agreement provided for a 20-member Regional Council, its working to be reviewed after ten years.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956?
o: At least two key portfolios for Telangana ministers
Recruitment to services by population ratio
A separate High Court for Telangana
q.x: The Agreement provided a Regional Council, a share of key portfolios and proportionate recruitment; it did not provide a separate High Court.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill received the assent of the President on:
q.x: The Lok Sabha passed it on 18 February, the Rajya Sabha on 20 February, and the President assented on 1 March 2014; 2 June was the appointed day.

q.s: The Group of Ministers on the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh (October 2013) was headed by:
q.x: Union Home Minister Sushil Kumar Shinde headed the GoM.

q.s: The Saka era began in the year:
q.x: The Saka era begins in 78 AD and is linked with Kanishka; the Vikrama Samvat begins in 57 BC.

q.s: Which of the following eras is NOT correctly matched with its starting year?
q.x: The Gupta era began in 319-320 AD.

q.s: Which of the following foreign groups came to India last?
q.x: The order of arrival was Indo-Greeks, Sakas, Parthians and then the Kushanas.

q.s: Which of the following statements about foreign groups in ancient India is correct?
o: The Kushanas came before the Sakas
The Parthians came before the Indo-Greeks
The Sakas came after the Kushanas
The Indo-Greeks came before the Sakas
q.x: The order is Indo-Greeks, Sakas, Parthians, Kushanas.

q.s: The phrase 'Italian of the East' for Telugu comes from the Italian traveller:
q.x: Niccolo de Conti (15th century) found Telugu words ending in vowels like Italian.

q.s: The Telugu script developed from the:
q.x: The Telugu-Kannada script grew out of the southern Brahmi script.

q.s: The Telugu word 'Vepuru' occurs in which inscription?
q.x: Vepuru occurs in the Myakadoni inscription; 'Nagabu' occurs at Amaravati.

q.s: The Satavahana king credited with making Sanskrit the royal language is:
q.x: Kuntala Satakarni is said to have made Sanskrit the court language.

q.s: Phanigiri, a Buddhist site where a pot of Ikshvaku lead coins was found in 2024, is in which district of Telangana?
q.x: Phanigiri lies in Suryapet district.

q.s: Kondapur, a fortified Satavahana town known for terracotta, beads and coins, is in which district?
q.x: Kondapur is in Sangareddy district (old Medak), not Khammam.

q.s: The Nanaghat inscription is associated with which Satavahana queen?
q.x: The Nanaghat inscription of Queen Naganika records the Vedic sacrifices of Satakarni I.

q.s: The amphitheatre at Nagarjunakonda (Vijayapuri) was used mainly for:
q.x: The amphitheatre was meant for performances and games, not for sacrifices.

q.s: The Ikshvaku king who performed the Asvamedha and Vajapeya sacrifices was:
q.x: Chamtamula (Santamula) I performed Vedic sacrifices while the royal ladies patronised Buddhism.

q.s: The Ikshvaku king Vasishthiputra Santamula was a worshipper of Mahasena, who is identified with:
q.x: Mahasena is Skanda; Santamula also worshipped Virupakshapati (Shiva).

q.s: Which of the following sacrifices was NOT performed by the Ikshvaku king Santamula?
q.x: Santamula performed the Ashvamedha, Rajasuya, Vajapeya and Agnistoma; Purushamedha is not recorded.

q.s: Which of the following Andhra dynasties came immediately after the Satavahanas?
q.x: The order is Satavahanas, Ikshvakus, Brihatpalayanas and Shalankayanas.

q.s: The capital of the Ikshvakus of Andhra was:
q.x: The Ikshvakus ruled from Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda).

q.s: Under the Vishnukundins, the biggest fort in the Telugu country was at:
q.x: Amrabad is noted as the biggest fort of the Vishnukundin period.

q.s: The official language of the Vishnukundin state was:
q.x: The Vishnukundins used Sanskrit as the official language.

q.s: Hala's Gathasaptasati, which contains Telugu words such as atta, potta and pilla, was written in:
q.x: The Gathasaptasati is a Maharashtri Prakrit anthology attributed to the Satavahana king Hala.

q.s: The first Telugu word 'Nagabu' was found in an inscription at:
q.x: 'Nagabu' was found at Amaravati; Vepuru occurs at Myakadoni.

q.s: Under the Kakatiyas, the 72 Niyogas (departments) were under the officer called:
q.x: The 72 Niyogas were supervised by the Bahattara Niyogadhipati.

q.s: The prime minister of the Kakatiya king Prataparudra II was:
q.x: Muppidi Nayudu served Prataparudra II; Malyala Hemadri Reddi served Ganapatideva.

q.s: The Reddi king Kumaragiri Reddi, who held the Vasantotsavam every year, was called:
q.x: Kumaragiri was called Karpura Vasantarayalu; Sarvajna Chakravarti was Pedakomati Vema's title.

q.s: The title 'Sarvajna Chakravarti' belonged to the Reddi king:
q.x: Pedakomati Vema, a scholar-king of Kondavidu, held the title Sarvajna Chakravarti.

q.s: Krishnadevaraya's campaign against the Gajapati Prataparudra began with the siege of:
q.x: Udayagiri (Nellore) fell after an 18-month siege in 1514.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the peace between Krishnadevaraya and Prataparudra Gajapati is correct?
o: The Gajapati became a vassal of the Bahmanis
Prataparudra's daughter was married to Krishnadevaraya
All lands north of the Godavari went to Vijayanagara
q.x: Annapurna Devi married Krishnadevaraya; lands north of the Krishna were returned to the Gajapati and Cuttack was not annexed.

q.s: Which of the following chronicles is NOT correctly matched with its subject?
q.x: Mirat-i-Sikandari is a history of Gujarat.

q.s: The 'Riyaz-ul-Insha' is a collection of the letters of:
q.x: Riyaz-ul-Insha holds the letters of the Bahmani minister Mahmud Gawan.

q.s: Under the Qutb Shahis, crown lands were known as:
q.x: Crown lands were Haveli; Dasabandhu lands paid only a tenth for maintaining tanks.

q.s: Under the Qutb Shahis, the officers called Mahasibs were in charge of:
q.x: Mahasibs looked after public morals; revenue was collected through tax farmers.

q.s: Golconda fort, originally a Kakatiya fort, was rebuilt by:
o: Sultan Quli and Ibrahim Qutb Shah
q.x: Sultan Quli and Ibrahim Qutb Shah rebuilt the old Kakatiya fort of Mankal.

q.s: The old name of Golconda was:
q.x: Golconda's old names were Mankal/Mangalavaram; Orugallu is Warangal.

q.s: Which of the Ashtadiggajas wrote 'Parijatapaharanamu' and was popularly known as Mukku Timmana?
q.x: Nandi Timmana wrote Parijatapaharanamu; Peddana wrote Manucharitra.

q.s: Which of the following poets was NOT one of the Ashtadiggajas of Krishnadevaraya's court?
q.x: Potana (15th century) predates Krishnadevaraya and was not an Ashtadiggaja.

q.s: The Tirumala Rayala Mahal (Tirumalai Nayak Palace) at Madurai was built by:
q.x: The palace was built by Tirumala Nayaka in the 17th century.

q.s: The founder of the Nayaka kingdom of Tanjore was:
q.x: Sevappa Nayaka founded the Tanjore Nayaka kingdom; Vishwanatha founded the Madurai line.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Jain centre in the Kakatiya region?
q.x: Bodhan, Vemulawada, Patancheru and Kolanupaka were Jain centres; Nagarjunakonda was a Buddhist centre.

q.s: The Padmakshi temple at Hanumakonda was originally a:
q.x: The Padmakshi temple was originally a Jain shrine.

q.s: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy, who rebelled against the British in 1846-47, belonged to present-day district of:
q.x: Uyyalawada is in the Kurnool region (now Nandyal district); he was hanged at Koilkuntla in 1847.

q.s: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy was sentenced to death in 1847 by the:
q.x: The Faujdari Adalat sentenced him to death in January 1847.

q.s: The Munagala estate, scene of a well-known anti-zamindari struggle, was held by the zamindar:
q.x: Munagala was under Nayani Venkataranga Rao; Challapalli was Yarlagadda Sivarama Prasad's estate.

q.s: Which leader, as APCC Secretary, authored the award that settled the Munagala struggle?
q.x: Gottipati Brahmaiah's award settled the Munagala struggle; he later chaired the AP Legislative Council (1964-68).

q.s: In 1982 Gottipati Brahmaiah was awarded the:
q.x: He received the Padma Bhushan, not the Padma Vibhushan.

q.s: PM-KISAN, under which eligible farmers get Rs 6,000 a year, is a:
o: Central sector scheme fully funded by the Centre
q.x: PM-KISAN is a central sector scheme; it was extended in 2026 without changing the Rs 6,000 benefit.

q.s: Which of the following statements about PM-KISAN is correct?
o: In 2026 it became a centrally sponsored scheme
In 2026 the Union Cabinet extended it to 2030-31
The benefit was raised to Rs 12,000 a year in 2026
States now bear 40% of its cost
q.x: It was extended to 2030-31 (outlay about Rs 3.15 lakh crore) and remains a central sector scheme of Rs 6,000 a year.

q.s: The collection of poems 'Mahaprasthanam' was written by:
q.x: Mahaprasthanam is Sri Sri's landmark revolutionary work, with a preface by Chalam.

q.s: The founding President of the Revolutionary Writers' Association (Virasam) in 1970 was:
q.x: Sri Sri headed Virasam on its founding in 1970.

q.s: The editorial column in Telugu journalism was introduced in 'Andhra Bhasha Sanjivani' by:
q.x: Kokkonda Venkataratnam ran Andhra Bhasha Sanjivani and introduced the editorial.

q.s: Which of the following Telugu journals is NOT correctly matched with the person associated with it?
o: Andhra Sahitya Parishad Patrika - Jayanti Ramayya
Andhra Bhasha Sanjivani - Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham
q.x: Andhra Bhasha Sanjivani was Kokkonda Venkataratnam's; Chilakamarti ran Manorama and Desamata.

q.s: The 'Lambadi' dance of Andhra Pradesh is performed by the:
q.x: Lambadi is the dance of the Banjara (Lambada) community.

q.s: Which of the following folk forms of Andhra Pradesh is NOT correctly matched with its feature?
o: Keelugurram - dance of the Banjara community
Lambadi - dance of the Banjara community
q.x: Keelugurram is the dummy-horse dance; Lambadi is the Banjara dance.

q.s: Among the Lambadis, Seethala Mata is worshipped during Seethala Panduga as a protection against:
q.x: Seethala Mata is worshipped to guard against smallpox.

q.s: The Revolutionary Writers' Association (Virasam) was founded on 4 July 1970 at:
q.x: Virasam was founded at Hyderabad; its first meeting was at Khammam.

q.s: The cultural troupe 'Art Lovers', founded by B. Narsinga Rao and Gaddar, was later renamed:
q.x: It became the Jana Natya Mandali in 1971; Praja Natya Mandali was the older IPTA-linked troupe.

q.s: In 1998 the Telugu University was renamed after:
q.x: It became the Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University in 1998.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Telugu University is correct?
o: It was set up under Act 27 of 1985
It was renamed after Kandukuri Veeresalingam
It was set up by an executive order
q.x: It was set up under Act 27 of 1985 and renamed after Potti Sreeramulu in 1998.

q.s: Mayurasharman, who was insulted at the Ghatika of Kanchi, went on to found the:
q.x: The Talagunda inscription tells how Mayurasharman founded the Kadamba kingdom.

q.s: Learning in the Pallava Ghatikas was carried on mainly in:
q.x: The ghatikas were Sanskrit centres of learning attached to temples.

q.s: Qutbuddin Aibak became the first Sultan of Delhi in 1206; his capital was:
q.x: Aibak ruled from Lahore; Iltutmish moved the capital to Delhi.

q.s: Before becoming Sultan, Qutbuddin Aibak held under Muhammad Ghori the post of:
q.x: Aibak, Ghori's slave, rose from Amir-i-Akhur to governor of his Indian conquests.

q.s: Prithviraj Chauhan was defeated by Muhammad Ghori in the Second Battle of Tarain in:
q.x: Prithviraj won the First Battle (1191) and lost the Second (1192).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Turkish conquest of north India is correct?
o: Prithviraj Chauhan won the Second Battle of Tarain
The Turks relied mainly on war elephants
Muhammad Ghori won the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192
North India was united under the Pratiharas in the 1190s
q.x: Prithviraj won the first battle (1191); Ghori won the second (1192) with mobile cavalry.

q.s: The presence of more elderly women, especially widows, among the aged population is called:
q.x: Feminisation of ageing means women outnumber men among the old.

q.s: Which is the first State in India to have a Senior Citizens' Welfare Department, a Commission and an Elderly Budget?
q.x: Kerala, with the oldest population, was the first.

q.s: According to Irawati Karve, which of the following is NOT a feature of North Indian kinship?
q.x: Cross-cousin marriage is a southern feature; the North practises gotra and village exogamy, and brides go to higher-status families.

q.s: The book 'Kinship Organisation in India' was written by:
q.x: Irawati Karve compared the kinship zones of India in this work.

q.s: The book 'Social Mobility' (1927), which set out vertical and horizontal mobility, was written by:
q.x: Sorokin's Social Mobility (1927) first distinguished vertical and horizontal mobility.

q.s: The concept of 'Kshatriyaisation' was given by:
q.x: Kulke described Kshatriyaisation; Srinivas gave Sanskritisation.

q.s: Article 371D of the Constitution contains special provisions for:
q.x: Article 371D deals with Andhra Pradesh (public employment and education); 371F is Sikkim, 371G Mizoram and 371H Arunachal.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Article and State is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Article 371F is for Sikkim; Mizoram is under 371G.

q.s: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 reserves for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies:
q.x: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam reserves one-third of seats for women.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the share of seats reserved for women in both panchayats and municipalities is:
q.x: Andhra Pradesh reserves 50% of seats for women in panchayats and municipalities alike.

q.s: Which city became India's first officially beggar-free city in 2025?
q.x: Indore was declared the first beggar-free city in 2025.

q.s: SMILE, which has a sub-scheme for rehabilitating persons engaged in begging, is run by the Ministry of:
q.x: SMILE is a scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

q.s: Under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, offences under the Act are:
q.x: Section 8 of the Act, as amended, makes offences non-bailable and non-compoundable.

q.s: The Dowry Prohibition Act was passed in the year:
q.x: The Dowry Prohibition Act dates from 1961; Section 498A of the IPC came in 1983.

q.s: According to NCRB data for 2023, the largest share of crimes against women was under the head:
q.x: Cruelty by husband or relatives (29.8%) led, followed by kidnapping and abduction (19.8%).

q.s: 'Young Bengal', regarded as India's first youth organisation, was founded by:
q.x: Derozio of Hindu College inspired the Young Bengal movement.

q.s: The first student-led national movement in India is regarded as the:
q.x: Students played a leading role in the Swadeshi Movement of 1905.

q.s: Under which Article can the President refer a question of law to the Supreme Court for its advisory opinion?
q.x: Article 143 gives the Supreme Court advisory jurisdiction; the opinion does not bind the President.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Article 143 is correct?
o: The Supreme Court's opinion on a reference is advisory and not binding on the President
Only the Prime Minister can make a reference
The Court cannot decline any reference
q.x: Article 143 gives only an advisory opinion.

q.s: In the Periodic Labour Force Survey, the Current Weekly Status records activity over a reference period of:
q.x: CWS uses the last seven days; usual status uses a year, and Current Daily Status each day of the week.

q.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is conducted by the:
q.x: PLFS is conducted by the NSO under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

q.s: Under the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA), free antenatal check-ups are given on:
q.x: PMSMA gives assured antenatal care on the 9th of every month.

q.s: Which of the following maternal health schemes is NOT correctly matched with its benefit?
o: PMSMA - free antenatal check-up on the 9th of every month
JSSK - free delivery, drugs and transport
Janani Suraksha Yojana - free antenatal check-up on the 9th of every month
q.x: JSY gives cash assistance for institutional delivery; the 9th-of-month check-up is PMSMA.

q.s: Under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, the certificate of identity is issued by the:
q.x: The District Magistrate issues the certificate of identity.

q.s: The Supreme Court recognised transgender persons as the 'third gender' in the case of:
o: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
q.x: The NALSA judgment (2014) recognised the third gender.

q.s: The 'Vibrant Villages Programme' is aimed at:
q.x: It develops northern border villages and checks out-migration.

q.s: Which of the following campaigns is NOT correctly matched with its focus?
o: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao - sex ratio and the girl child
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan - sex ratio and the girl child
q.x: Nasha Mukt Bharat targets substance abuse among youth.

q.s: The Ganga Water Treaty of 1996 between India and Bangladesh provides for sharing of waters at:
q.x: The treaty covers Ganga waters at Farakka for 30 years; the Teesta is still unsettled.

q.s: The Ganga Water Treaty of 1996 between India and Bangladesh was signed for a period of:
q.x: The treaty runs for 30 years.

q.s: The first Secretary-General of the United Nations, Trygve Lie, belonged to:
q.x: Trygve Lie (1946-52) was Norwegian; Dag Hammarskjold was Swedish.

q.s: Which UN Secretary-General is NOT correctly matched with his country?
q.x: Dag Hammarskjold was Swedish.

q.s: Which World Bank Group institution provides political-risk guarantees to foreign investors?
q.x: MIGA gives political-risk insurance; the IMF does not.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the IMF is correct?
o: It gives short-term balance-of-payments support, not project finance
It provides political-risk guarantees to investors
It is a part of the WTO
q.x: Project finance is the World Bank's role and political-risk guarantees are MIGA's.

q.s: The UN peacekeeping mission MONUSCO operates in:
q.x: MONUSCO is in the DR Congo; UNMISS is in South Sudan.

q.s: Which of the following UN peacekeeping missions is NOT correctly matched with its location?
q.x: MINURCAT (2007-10) was in the Central African Republic and Chad.

q.s: NATGRID functions under the:
q.x: NATGRID is under the MHA; RAW is under the Cabinet Secretariat.

q.s: Which of the following does NOT function under the Ministry of Home Affairs?
q.x: RAW is under the Cabinet Secretariat.

q.s: Which of the following Articles does NOT directly confer the power of judicial review on courts?
q.x: Articles 13, 32 and 226 are the bases of judicial review; Article 368 deals with amending the Constitution.

q.s: The Indian Constitution, in terms of amendment, is best described as:
o: As rigid as the US Constitution
A blend of rigidity and flexibility
q.x: Some parts are amended by simple majority, some by special majority, some also need State ratification.

q.s: Under dyarchy introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919, which of the following was a transferred subject?
q.x: Local self-government, education and health were transferred; irrigation, police and land revenue were reserved.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a reserved subject under provincial dyarchy (1919)?
q.x: Education was a transferred subject.

q.s: The Government of India Act, 1919 created the office of the:
o: Public Service Commission of the Provinces
High Commissioner for India in London
q.x: The 1919 Act created the High Commissioner for India in London.

q.s: The first Chancellor of the Chamber of Princes (1921) was the Maharaja of:
q.x: Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner was the first Chancellor.

q.s: The national motto 'Satyameva Jayate' is taken from the:
q.x: Satyameva Jayate comes from the Mundaka Upanishad.

q.s: Which of the following national symbols of India is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The national tree is the banyan; the mango is the national fruit.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Constituent Assembly of India is correct?
o: Mahatma Gandhi was one of its members
Its members were directly elected by the people
M.A. Jinnah led the Muslim League bloc in it
Christians, Anglo-Indians and Parsis were represented in it
q.x: Minorities were represented; members were indirectly elected by provincial assemblies, and neither Gandhi nor Jinnah was a member.

q.s: The members of the Constituent Assembly from the provinces were elected by the:
q.x: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, provincial assemblies elected members by single transferable vote.

q.s: The word 'Secular' was added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the:
q.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity'.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Indian secularism is NOT correct?
o: The State gives equal respect to all religions
The word 'Secular' was added by the 42nd Amendment
The Constituent Assembly rejected adding 'God' to the Preamble
It means a strict wall of separation between State and religion
q.x: Indian secularism is equal respect for all religions, not the US-style wall of separation.

q.s: Under Article 358, Article 19 is suspended automatically when a National Emergency is declared on the ground of:
q.x: Article 19 is suspended automatically only for war or external aggression, not armed rebellion.

q.s: Which Article empowers Parliament to restrict the Fundamental Rights of members of the armed forces?
q.x: Article 33 lets Parliament restrict the rights of the armed forces, police and similar forces.

q.s: The writ issued by a higher court to stop a lower court from exceeding its jurisdiction while proceedings are pending is:
q.x: Prohibition is purely preventive; Certiorari can also quash an order already passed.

q.s: Which writ can be both preventive and curative?
q.x: Certiorari can be issued to quash an order already passed as well as to prevent excess of jurisdiction.

q.s: The 'basic structure' doctrine of the Constitution was laid down in the case of:
q.x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that Parliament cannot alter the basic structure.

q.s: Which of the following cases is NOT correctly matched with its subject?
o: Indra Sawhney - 50 per cent ceiling on reservation
Minerva Mills - balance between Fundamental Rights and DPSP
q.x: Bommai dealt with Article 356, floor tests and secularism.

q.s: Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, the preliminary assessment of a child aged 16-18 accused of a heinous offence is made by the:
q.x: The JJ Board makes the preliminary assessment; the CWC deals with children in need of care.

q.s: After the 2021 amendment of the Juvenile Justice Act, adoption orders are issued by the:
q.x: The 2021 amendment moved adoption orders from courts to the District Magistrate.

q.s: The amendment of which of the following does NOT need ratification by half of the States?
q.x: Fundamental Rights such as Article 32 need only a special majority; the federal provisions also need State ratification.

q.s: On the prorogation of a House of Parliament, the Bills pending before it:
o: Are sent to a Joint Committee
q.x: Bills survive prorogation; only pending notices (except for introduction of Bills) lapse. Bills lapse on dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the lapse of Bills is correct?
o: A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha and not passed by the Lok Sabha does not lapse on dissolution of the Lok Sabha
All pending Bills lapse on prorogation
Bills pending in the Lok Sabha survive its dissolution
Prorogation of a House is done by its presiding officer
q.x: Bills survive prorogation; on dissolution Bills pending in the Lok Sabha lapse; prorogation is by the President.

q.s: Following the Berubari reference (1960), the cession of Indian territory to Pakistan was given effect through the:
q.x: The Supreme Court held cession needs an Article 368 amendment, hence the 9th Amendment (1960).

q.s: The 100th Constitutional Amendment Act (2015) gave effect to the land boundary agreement between India and:
q.x: The 100th Amendment gave effect to the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement; Katchatheevu went to Sri Lanka without an amendment.

q.s: A person who is not a member of Parliament may be appointed Prime Minister, but must become a member of either House within:
q.x: He must become a member of either House, not only the Lok Sabha, within six months.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Prime Minister of India is correct?
o: There is no limit on the number of terms he can serve
He can hold office for at most two terms
He must be a member of the Lok Sabha only
He is elected directly by the people
q.x: The Constitution fixes no term limit for the Prime Minister.

q.s: The first Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly (1956) was:
q.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker; Kalluri Subbarao the first Deputy Speaker.

q.s: Which of the following first office-holders of the Andhra Pradesh Legislature is NOT correctly matched?
o: First woman Speaker - K. Prathibha Bharathi
First Chairman of the Legislative Council - K. Prathibha Bharathi
q.x: The first Council Chairman was Madapati Hanumantha Rao.

q.s: The date of the election of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is fixed by the:
q.x: The President fixes the date; the Lok Sabha elects its Speaker from among its members under Article 93.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is correct?
o: Only a sitting member of the Lok Sabha can be elected Speaker
The Speaker takes a separate oath as Speaker
A non-member may be elected if he becomes a member within six months
The Speaker is elected by both Houses of Parliament
q.x: The Speaker is chosen from among the Lok Sabha's members and takes no separate oath.

q.s: The case S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) is mainly concerned with:
q.x: Bommai laid down limits on Article 356, including the floor test and judicial review.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the S.R. Bommai judgment is correct?
o: It was decided by a five-judge Bench
The Assembly may be dissolved only after Parliament approves the proclamation
The proclamation under Article 356 is beyond judicial review
Majority may be tested at the Raj Bhavan
q.x: Until approval the Assembly is only kept in suspended animation; the Bench had nine judges.

q.s: Under the Tenth Schedule, a question of disqualification of a Lok Sabha member on the ground of defection is decided by the:
q.x: The Speaker (or Chairman) decides defection cases; general disqualifications are decided by the President on the EC's opinion.

q.s: The disqualifications for membership of Parliament are dealt with in:
q.x: Article 102 covers Parliament; Article 191 covers State Legislatures.

q.s: Members of Parliament enjoy freedom from arrest in civil cases during a session and for how many days before and after it?
q.x: Freedom from arrest in civil cases extends 40 days before and after a session; it does not apply to criminal cases.

q.s: Which of the following statements about parliamentary privileges is correct?
o: Freedom from arrest applies to criminal cases too
The right to be told of a member's arrest is an individual privilege
A House can punish both members and outsiders for breach of privilege
All privileges have been codified by law
q.x: The right to information of arrest is a collective privilege; freedom from arrest covers only civil cases.

q.s: Judges of a High Court are appointed by the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
q.x: High Court judges are appointed by the President after consultation as laid down in Article 217.

q.s: The convention of appointing the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court as Chief Justice of India was broken in:
q.x: It was broken in 1973 (A.N. Ray) and again in 1977 (M.H. Beg).

q.s: The first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India was:
q.x: Fathima Beevi was appointed in 1989; Leila Seth was the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court.

q.s: After retirement, Justice Fathima Beevi served as the Governor of:
q.x: She became Governor of Tamil Nadu.

q.s: The case Divisional Manager, Aravali Golf Club v. Chander Hass (2007) is cited as an instance of:
q.x: The Court held that judges must not encroach upon the domain of the legislature or executive.

q.s: Part XIV-A (Tribunals) was inserted in the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The Swaran Singh Committee recommended Part XIV-A (Articles 323A and 323B).

q.s: Which of the following statements about tribunals in the Constitution is correct?
o: Part XIV-A was inserted by the 44th Amendment
Tribunal chairpersons generally get the status of Supreme Court judges
Article 323-B deals only with service matters
Part XIV-A contains only Articles 323-A and 323-B
q.x: Part XIV-A (42nd Amendment) has two Articles; chairpersons generally get High Court judge status.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT abolished by the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021?
q.x: The Act abolished the IPAB, FCAT and others, moving their work to High Courts; the NGT continues.

q.s: The National Emergency of 1975 was proclaimed on:
q.x: The Emergency on the ground of internal disturbance was proclaimed on 25 June 1975.

q.s: After the 44th Amendment, the President can proclaim a National Emergency only on the:
o: Oral advice of the Prime Minister
Written advice of the Union Cabinet
q.x: The 44th Amendment requires the written advice of the Cabinet.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the post-retirement employment of the UPSC Chairman is correct?
o: He can be appointed a State Governor only
He can become a member of a State PSC
He cannot take any further government job
q.x: The UPSC Chairman is barred from any further employment under the Government of India or a State.

q.s: 'A Vindication of the Rights of Woman' (1792) was written by:
q.x: Wollstonecraft wrote the Vindication; Olympe de Gouges wrote the Declaration of the Rights of Woman (1791).

q.s: Which of the following thinkers is NOT correctly matched with the work or idea?
o: Olympe de Gouges - A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
Mary Wollstonecraft - A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
John Locke - natural rights to life, liberty and property
q.x: Olympe de Gouges wrote the Declaration of the Rights of Woman (1791).

q.s: The Central Bureau of Investigation was set up in 1963 on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The CBI was set up by a Home Ministry resolution on 1 April 1963.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the CBI is correct?
o: It was created by the DSPE Act, 1946
It works under the Ministry of Home Affairs
It is not a statutory body
q.x: The CBI was set up by an executive resolution; it draws its powers from the DSPE Act and is under the DoPT.

q.s: The founder Director of the CBI was:
q.x: D.P. Kohli was the founder Director; the CBI motto is 'Industry, Impartiality, Integrity'.

q.s: Since the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 has not been brought into force, whistle-blower complaints are handled by the:
q.x: The CVC acts under the 2004 PIDPI resolution.

q.s: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 under Article 263 on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The Presidential order of 28 May 1990 followed the Sarkaria Commission.

q.s: The Inter-State Council is chaired by the:
q.x: The Prime Minister chairs the Inter-State Council.

q.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission (award period 2026-31) was chaired by:
q.x: Arvind Panagariya chaired the 16th FC; N.K. Singh chaired the 15th.

q.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission kept the States' share of the divisible pool of central taxes at:
q.x: It retained 41%; 42% was the 14th FC's share.

q.s: The conditions for recognition of a national party are laid down in the:
q.x: Paragraph 6B of the Symbols Order, 1968 lays down the conditions.

q.s: A party recognised as a State party in how many States qualifies as a national party?
q.x: Recognition as a State party in four or more States is enough by itself.

q.s: The NOTA option was introduced on the direction of the Supreme Court in the case of:
o: Lily Thomas v. Union of India
Common Cause v. Union of India
q.x: PUCL (2013) linked the secret negative vote to Article 19(1)(a).

q.s: Which of the following statements about NOTA is correct?
o: A fresh poll is held if NOTA gets the most votes
NOTA is available in Rajya Sabha elections
Even if NOTA gets the most votes, the leading candidate wins
NOTA was introduced by a constitutional amendment
q.x: NOTA has no effect on the result; the Supreme Court barred it in Rajya Sabha polls (2018).

q.s: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, relating to simultaneous elections, inserts a new:
q.x: The 'One Nation One Election' Bill inserts Article 82A and amends Articles 83, 172 and 327.

q.s: Which of the following States does NOT have Panchayati Raj Institutions?
q.x: Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram have no PRIs; they have traditional councils.

q.s: The three-tier Panchayati Raj system was recommended by the:
q.x: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended democratic decentralisation in three tiers.

q.s: Under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, the consent of what percentage of affected families is needed for land acquisition for private projects?
q.x: Private projects need 80% consent, PPP projects 70%.

q.s: Under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, which of the following is mandatory for land acquisition?
q.x: A Social Impact Assessment is mandatory.

q.s: Under the Van Dhan Vikas Kendras, at least what share of members must be from the Scheduled Tribes?
q.x: Each Kendra of about 15 SHGs must have at least 60% ST members.

q.s: The NAMASTE scheme (2022) aims at:
o: Ending manual sewer and septic tank cleaning
q.x: NAMASTE seeks the safety and dignity of sanitation workers and ends hazardous manual cleaning.

q.s: The Reserve Bank of India was set up on 1 April 1935 and nationalised in:
q.x: The RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949.

q.s: Which of the following regulators is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: IBBI works under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

q.s: The National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP) was launched in August 2021 by:
q.x: NITI Aayog launched NMP 1.0 worth about Rs 6 lakh crore.

q.s: Under NMP 2.0 (FY26-FY30), the sector with the largest share of assets is:
q.x: Highways form the largest share (about 26%) of NMP 2.0's Rs 16.72 lakh crore.

q.s: MeeSeva, the single-window G2C service centres of Andhra Pradesh, were launched in 2011 under Chief Minister:
q.x: MeeSeva began in 2011 under Kiran Kumar Reddy.

q.s: The Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) of Andhra Pradesh was set up in:
q.x: RTGS (2017) runs a Data Lake and a Command and Control Centre.

q.s: UDAN, the regional air connectivity scheme, is implemented by the Ministry of:
q.x: UDAN uses capped fares and viability gap funding.

q.s: PM Gati Shakti, launched in October 2021, is a:
o: GIS-based National Master Plan for multimodal connectivity
q.x: Gati Shakti integrates infrastructure planning across ministries on a GIS platform.

q.s: Disinvestment of a public sector undertaking refers to:
o: Sale of part of the government's equity
Transfer of PSU to a State government
q.x: Disinvestment is the sale of part of the State's equity and need not transfer management.

q.s: Which of the following statements about disinvestment is correct?
o: It is the purchase of private shares by the government
It can be done only by strategic sale
It need not transfer ownership or management of the PSU
q.x: Disinvestment is the sale of part of the government's equity.

q.s: The Pokhran-II nuclear tests of May 1998 (Operation Shakti) were conducted when the Prime Minister was:
q.x: Pokhran-II took place under Vajpayee; Pokhran-I (1974) was under Indira Gandhi.

q.s: After Pokhran-II, the US imposed sanctions on India under the:
q.x: The Glenn Amendment sanctions followed the 1998 tests; talks between Jaswant Singh and Strobe Talbott came later.

q.s: The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is calculated as:
o: Sum of the headcount ratio and intensity
Product of the headcount ratio and intensity of poverty
Average of the three HDI indices
q.x: MPI = H x A, using the Alkire-Foster method.

q.s: Under the global MPI, a person is considered multidimensionally poor if deprived in at least:
q.x: The poverty cut-off is one-third of weighted indicators.

q.s: The Capability Poverty Measure (Human Development Report 1996) used which of the following indicators?
q.x: The CPM used underweight children under 5, births unattended by trained personnel and female illiteracy.

q.s: The Human Poverty Index meant for developed countries (HPI-2) added which of the following to the HPI-1 indicators?
q.x: HPI-2 added income poverty and long-term unemployment.

q.s: Assam's Small Family Norms (from 2021) bar parents of more than two children from:
q.x: The norm applies to State government jobs, not Lok Sabha elections.

q.s: The draft Uttar Pradesh Population Bill (July 2021) was released by the:
q.x: The UP State Law Commission released the draft Bill.

q.s: The Census of India records migration on the basis of:
o: Place of birth and place of last residence
q.x: The Census uses both place of birth and place of last residence.

q.s: As per Census 2011 (place of last residence), the largest inter-State female migration stream was:
q.x: Urban-Urban was the largest inter-State female stream by last residence.

q.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission (2026-31), the share of urban local bodies in local body grants is:
q.x: The 16th FC raised the urban share to 45% from 36%; rural bodies get 55%.

q.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission splits local body grants into basic and performance grants in the ratio:
q.x: Grants are 80% basic and 20% performance.

q.s: The Madanapalle Water Grid in Andhra Pradesh is meant mainly for:
q.x: Madanapalle lies in Rayalaseema, the target of the grid.

q.s: The Village and Ward Secretariat system of Andhra Pradesh was launched on 2 October 2019 at:
q.x: It was launched at Karapa with about 1.26 lakh staff.

q.s: 'Mana Badi Nadu-Nedu' programme of Andhra Pradesh (2019) is meant for:
q.x: Nadu-Nedu ('then and now') modernises government schools.

q.s: The LEAP programme in Andhra Pradesh schools responds to learning gaps reported by:
q.x: LEAP addresses the learning gaps highlighted by ASER.

q.s: 'YSR Shaadi Tohfa' of Andhra Pradesh gives marriage assistance to brides from the:
q.x: Shaadi Tohfa is for minority brides; Kalyanamasthu covers SC, ST, BC and others.

q.s: Under YSR Kalyanamasthu, the marriage assistance for SC/ST brides is:
q.x: SC/ST brides get Rs 1 lakh, BC brides Rs 50,000; both bride and groom must have passed SSC.

q.s: Under the Eleventh Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the highest priority in water use is given to:
q.x: The Schedule's principles for the Godavari and Krishna boards put drinking water first.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, which bodies were constituted to manage the river waters of the two States?
o: Godavari and Krishna Water Disputes Tribunals
Godavari and Krishna River Management Boards
q.x: Section 85 set up the two River Management Boards.

q.s: Transfer payments such as old age pensions are:
o: Excluded from both national and personal income
Excluded from national income but added to personal income
q.x: Transfer payments are one-way payments with no productive service in return.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT included in national income?
q.x: Pensions are transfer payments; wages, rent and profits are factor incomes.

q.s: As per the NSSO 70th round (2013), agricultural households formed about what share of rural households?
q.x: Agricultural households were about 57.8% of rural households - a majority.

q.s: Which sector has the highest share of India's total employment?
q.x: Agriculture still has the largest share of employment, though it is falling.

q.s: As per the IMF World Economic Outlook, India's rank in GDP at purchasing power parity is:
q.x: India is third at PPP, after China and the USA.

q.s: As per the IMF World Economic Outlook (April 2026), India's rank in nominal GDP was:
q.x: India was ranked 6th in nominal GDP.

q.s: The 'Bombay Plan' of 1944 was prepared by:
q.x: J.R.D. Tata, G.D. Birla and six others prepared the Bombay Plan.

q.s: Which of the following pre-independence plans is NOT correctly matched with its author?
q.x: The Gandhian Plan (1944) was drafted by Shriman Narayan Agarwal.

q.s: The Second Five Year Plan (1956-61) was based on the model of:
q.x: The Second Plan used the Mahalanobis model, stressing heavy industry and the public sector.

q.s: The targets of the Second Five Year Plan had to be pruned because of:
q.x: A foreign exchange crisis in 1957-58 forced the pruning of targets.

q.s: India's current account deficit peaked at about 4.8% of GDP in:
q.x: The CAD peaked in 2012-13; in 1990-91 it was about 3%.

q.s: The National Renewal Fund, set up in February 1992, was meant to:
o: Provide a safety net for workers affected by industrial restructuring
q.x: The NRF funded retraining, redeployment and compensation of affected workers.

q.s: Under Article 270 of the Constitution, taxes are:
o: Levied and collected by the Union and shared with the States
Levied by the Union and collected by the States
Levied and collected by the States
Surcharges kept wholly by the Union
q.x: Article 270 creates the shareable pool distributed on Finance Commission advice.

q.s: Which Article provides for surcharges on taxes wholly for the purposes of the Union?
q.x: Article 271 surcharges are not shared with the States.

q.s: GST on supplies in the course of inter-State trade (IGST) is levied and collected by the Union under:
q.x: Article 269A covers IGST, apportioned between the Union and States.

q.s: Which of the following Articles is NOT correctly matched with the tax arrangement it provides?
o: Article 268 - duties levied by the Union, collected and kept by the States
Article 270 - taxes shared with States on Finance Commission advice
Article 269 - taxes kept wholly by the Union
q.x: Article 269 taxes are levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States.

q.s: The Chairperson of NITI Aayog is the:
q.x: The Prime Minister chairs NITI Aayog; the Vice-Chairperson is appointed by him.

q.s: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on:
q.x: NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015.

q.s: The SDG India Index is brought out by:
q.x: NITI Aayog brings out the SDG India Index (first, Baseline Report 2018).

q.s: The SDG India Index Baseline Report 2018 scored how many of the 17 SDGs?
q.x: SDGs 12, 13, 14 and 17 were left out, leaving 13.

q.s: In the JAM trinity, the letter 'M' stands for:
q.x: JAM = Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and Mobile.

q.s: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana was launched in:
q.x: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014.

q.s: Regional Rural Banks were set up on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The Narasimham Working Group (1975) recommended RRBs.

q.s: The share capital of a Regional Rural Bank is held by the Centre, the sponsor bank and the State Government in the ratio:
q.x: Centre 50%, sponsor bank 35%, State 15%.

q.s: After LIC bought a majority stake in IDBI Bank in 2019, the RBI reclassified IDBI Bank as a:
q.x: IDBI Bank was recategorised as a private sector lender.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the sale of stake in IDBI Bank is correct?
o: Only the Government is selling its stake
Both the Government and LIC are selling their stakes
Only LIC is selling its stake
IDBI Bank is classified as a public sector bank
q.x: Both the Government and LIC are selling; the RBI treats IDBI Bank as a private sector lender.

q.s: The S.S. Tarapore Committee-II (2006) dealt with:
o: Financial sector reforms - 'A Hundred Small Steps'
q.x: Tarapore-II was on fuller capital account convertibility.

q.s: Which of the following committees is NOT correctly matched with its subject?
o: Tarapore Committee-II - fuller capital account convertibility
Rakesh Mohan (CFSA) - self-assessment of the financial sector
M.S. Verma Committee - fuller capital account convertibility
Raghuram Rajan Committee - 'A Hundred Small Steps'
q.x: The M.S. Verma Committee (1999) set parameters to identify weak public sector banks.

q.s: The Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) is compiled by the:
q.x: The Labour Bureau, Shimla, under the Labour Ministry compiles CPI-IW.

q.s: The current base year of CPI-IW, revised in September 2020, is:
q.x: The base was moved from 2001 to 2016.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT revenue expenditure of the government?
q.x: Repayment of loans is capital expenditure; interest and salaries are revenue expenditure.

q.s: Debt owed by the government in foreign currency to foreign lenders is called:
q.x: Foreign-currency obligations belong to external debt; internal debt is borrowed within the country.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of internal debt?
o: Its source is the domestic economy
It is owed in foreign currency to foreign lenders
It is raised by domestic borrowing
It includes market loans such as dated securities
q.x: Foreign-currency obligations form external debt.

q.s: Under the RBI Act, the Monetary Policy Committee is required to meet at least:
q.x: The MPC must meet at least four times a year; in practice it meets every two months.

q.s: The Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI has how many members?
q.x: It has six members: three from the RBI and three external members.

q.s: Which of the following statements about tax buoyancy and tax elasticity is correct?
o: Elasticity includes discretionary changes; buoyancy excludes them
Both measure the change in GDP due to tax
Buoyancy includes the effect of discretionary changes in tax rates; elasticity excludes it
q.x: Buoyancy captures total revenue response including policy changes; elasticity measures only automatic response.

q.s: Under the current GST structure, gold, silver and jewellery attract GST at:
q.x: Gold and jewellery are at 3%; rough diamonds at 0.25%.

q.s: Which of the following items is NOT correctly matched with its GST rate under the current structure?
o: Most items of the old 12% slab - 5%
q.x: Rough diamonds attract 0.25%.

q.s: In India's trade agreements, the abbreviation CEPA stands for:
q.x: CEPA is Partnership; CECA is Cooperation.

q.s: Which country joined when SAPTA was replaced by SAFTA (2006)?
q.x: Afghanistan joined SAARC in 2007 and SAFTA thereafter; the Maldives was an original SAPTA member.

q.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Development Policy 4.0, the target for FDI is at least:
q.x: The policy targets FDI of at least $10 billion.

q.s: The only genetically modified crop approved for commercial cultivation in India is:
q.x: Bt cotton was approved in 2002; Bt brinjal is under moratorium since 2010.

q.s: In 2010, a moratorium was imposed on the commercial release of:
q.x: The moratorium of 2010 was on Bt brinjal.

q.s: About what share of India's net sown area is rainfed?
q.x: Roughly half of the net sown area is rainfed.

q.s: Which crop has the lowest share of its area under irrigation among the following?
q.x: Only about 26% of pulses area is irrigated, against about 67% for rice.

q.s: The ICAR National Agricultural Research Project (NARP) divided India into how many agro-climatic zones?
q.x: NARP has 127 zones; the Planning Commission had 15 zones and 72 sub-zones.

q.s: The Planning Commission divided India into how many agro-climatic regions?
q.x: The Planning Commission's classification had 15 agro-climatic regions.

q.s: Seed Replacement Rate (SRR) refers to the percentage of a crop's area sown with:
o: Certified/quality seed instead of farm-saved seed
q.x: SRR is the share sown with certified seed; VRR counts area under recently released varieties.

q.s: Under the 'Seed Village' concept, farmers are given:
o: Loans to buy seed from companies
Foundation seed and training to produce certified seed locally
q.x: Seed Villages aim at local production of quality seed.

q.s: Land Tribunals under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973 are headed by the:
q.x: The RDO heads the Land Tribunals.

q.s: Under the AP Land Ceiling Act, 1973, benami transfers made after which date are ignored?
q.x: Transfers after 30 January 1970 are disregarded.

q.s: Price spread in agricultural marketing refers to:
o: Difference between MSP and market price
Difference between wholesale and export prices
Difference between the price paid by the consumer and the price received by the farmer
q.x: Price spread measures the marketing margins between farmer and consumer.

q.s: The National Commission on Farmers suggested that a regulated market should be available to farmers within about:
q.x: The NCF (Swaminathan) suggested a regulated market within about 5 km.

q.s: In the CACP cost concepts, the fullest cost including rent on owned land and interest on fixed capital is:
q.x: C2 = A2 + FL + rent on owned land + interest on owned fixed capital.

q.s: Which of the following CACP cost concepts is NOT correctly matched?
o: FL - imputed value of family labour
A2+FL - paid-out cost plus family labour
A2 - imputed value of family labour
q.x: A2 is the actual paid-out cost.

q.s: The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act came into force on:
q.x: The MSMED Act came into force on 2 October 2006.

q.s: The composite criterion of investment and turnover for classifying MSMEs took effect from:
q.x: It was notified on 1 June 2020 and took effect from 1 July 2020.

q.s: The WTO classifies services using the:
q.x: The WTO uses the UNCPC; the NIC is India's own classification by MoSPI.

q.s: In the Indian Constitution, education and electricity are placed in the:
q.x: Education and electricity are Concurrent subjects; health is in the State List.

q.s: Section 94 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 provides for:
o: Creation of the new capital Amaravati
Fiscal measures including tax incentives to promote industrialisation
q.x: Section 94(1) gives tax incentives; 94(3) and others cover backward-area grants and capital support.

q.s: The backward-area development programmes under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 cover seven districts of:
q.x: The seven districts are 4 in Rayalaseema and 3 in North Coastal Andhra.

q.s: In fish production, Andhra Pradesh ranks:
q.x: Andhra Pradesh is India's leading fish-producing State.

q.s: Which region of Andhra Pradesh is being developed as the 'Horticulture Hub'?
q.x: Rayalaseema is being developed as the Horticulture Hub.

q.s: As per Census 2011, the sex ratio of Andhra Pradesh (residual State) is:
q.x: AP's sex ratio is 997 (India 943); its child sex ratio is 944.

q.s: Which of the following Census 2011 figures for Andhra Pradesh is NOT correct?
q.x: AP's child sex ratio is 944.

q.s: Under Special Category Status, the Centre bears what share of the cost of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
q.x: Special Category States get 90:10 funding against 60:40 for others.

q.s: Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh (for five years) was promised by the Prime Minister in 2014 on the floor of the:
q.x: Dr Manmohan Singh made the promise in the Rajya Sabha.

q.s: APCNF, the natural farming programme of Andhra Pradesh, stands for:
o: Andhra Pradesh Crop and Nutrient Fund
q.x: APCNF is run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha; it uses mulching and bio-inputs.

q.s: The Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) was launched in:
q.x: MIDH (2014-15) merged NHM and HMNEH as sub-schemes.

q.s: Under MIDH, the Centre:State funding ratio for general States is:
q.x: General States share 60:40; NE and Himalayan States 90:10.

q.s: Which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh is known as the 'rice bowl' and an aquaculture hub?
q.x: The Godavari Zone is the rice bowl of the State.

q.s: Which of the following agro-climatic zones of Andhra Pradesh is NOT correctly matched?
o: Scarce Rainfall Zone - chief paddy-growing zone
North Coastal Zone - high rainfall and laterite soils
Godavari Zone - rice bowl and aquaculture
High Altitude and Tribal Zone - coffee
q.x: The Scarce Rainfall Zone grows groundnut and dryland crops.

q.s: As per the 20th Livestock Census (2019), India's total livestock population was about:
q.x: The 20th Census counted 535.78 million livestock.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the 21st Livestock Census is correct?
o: It covered only cattle and buffaloes
It covered 16 species and 219 indigenous breeds
It covered only exotic and crossbred breeds
It was India's first livestock census
q.x: The 21st Census covered 16 species including 219 indigenous breeds.

q.s: Asia's first Export Processing Zone was set up in 1965 at:
q.x: Kandla (Gulf of Kutch, 1965) was Asia's first EPZ; SEEPZ came in 1973.

q.s: India's first private-sector Export Processing Zone (1997) was set up at:
q.x: Surat was the first private EPZ.

q.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's free power scheme, farm pump sets get free power for:
q.x: Farmers get 9 hours of free daytime power.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the power sector of Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: T&D losses fell from 12.10% in 2014-15 to 9.32% in 2024-25
Farm pump sets get free power only at night
Peak demand has never crossed 10,000 MW
q.x: T&D losses have fallen; peak demand reached 15,016 MW in May 2026.

q.s: The first of Andhra Pradesh's principal e-governance platforms, introduced in 1998 for property registration, was:
q.x: CARD (1998) came first, then eSeva (2001) and MeeSeva (2011).

q.s: SISFS, under Startup India, provides:
q.x: The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme funds proof of concept, prototypes and market entry.

q.s: Which of the following Startup India initiatives is NOT correctly matched with its purpose?
o: Startup India Hub - single online platform
q.x: The Yatra is a talent hunt in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.

q.s: The National Indicator Framework for monitoring the SDGs in India is developed by:
q.x: MoSPI develops the NIF; NITI Aayog coordinates SDGs and prepares the SDG India Index.

q.s: Which planet rotates from east to west (retrograde rotation), like Uranus?
q.x: Venus and Uranus have retrograde rotation.

q.s: The brightest planet as seen from the Earth is:
q.x: Venus is the brightest planet; only the Sun and the Moon are brighter.

q.s: The Andes mountains were formed by the subduction of which plate under the South American plate?
q.x: The Nazca plate subducts beneath South America.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its plate setting?
o: Andes - subduction of the Nazca plate
q.x: The Sagaing Fault in Myanmar is a transform boundary between the Indian and Eurasian plates.

q.s: The magnetic striping of the ocean floor, supporting sea-floor spreading, was explained in 1963 by:
q.x: Vine and Matthews explained the symmetric magnetic bands; Hess proposed sea-floor spreading.

q.s: The age of the oceanic crust, moving away from a mid-ocean ridge:
q.x: Crust is youngest at the ridge and gets older and thicker away from it.

q.s: The Latur earthquake occurred in Maharashtra in the year:
q.x: Latur was hit in 1993; the Bhuj earthquake was in 2001.

q.s: On the Richter scale, each whole-number step represents an increase in energy released of about:
q.x: Each step is 10 times the amplitude and about 31.6 times the energy.

q.s: The Richter scale for measuring earthquakes is:
q.x: The Richter scale is a logarithmic scale of magnitude.

q.s: Acidic (felsic) lava is:
q.x: Acidic lava is silica-rich and viscous, giving explosive eruptions and steep cones.

q.s: Which type of volcanic landform is formed by basic, fluid lava?
q.x: Fluid basic lava spreads widely to build gently sloping shield volcanoes.

q.s: A single funnel-shaped, drowned river mouth with a free connection to the sea is called:
q.x: An estuary is a drowned river mouth where tides prevent delta formation.

q.s: Which of the following does NOT favour the formation of a delta?
o: Shallow sea at the river mouth
q.x: Strong tides and currents carry the sediment away, so estuaries form instead.

q.s: In karst landforms, a small closed funnel-shaped depression is called a:
q.x: The doline is the commonest karst landform; uvalas form by joined dolines.

q.s: A large flat-floored depression in karst regions is called a:
q.x: A polje is a large flat-floored depression.

q.s: One nautical mile is equal to:
q.x: A nautical mile is 1,852 m; 1,609 m is the statute (land) mile.

q.s: One fathom, used to measure the depth of water, is equal to:
q.x: A fathom is 6 feet (about 1.83 m).

q.s: The river known as the 'Oil River', which forms an inland delta in Mali, is the:
q.x: The Niger rises in the Fouta Djallon and enters the Gulf of Guinea.

q.s: The river Niger enters the Atlantic Ocean through the:
q.x: The Niger forms its delta on the Gulf of Guinea in Nigeria.

q.s: Angel Falls, the highest waterfall in the world, is located in:
q.x: Angel Falls (979 m) is on the Churun river in Venezuela.

q.s: Which of the following waterfalls is NOT correctly matched with its location?
q.x: Tugela, the second highest, is in South Africa.
